Query Methods

findMany, findUnique, create — one object per model, named after it, with methods that return Promises.

The generated client exposes one property per model from schema.prisma, lower-cased — prisma.user, prisma.ticket, prisma.tag, and so on — each with the same family of query methods. A few used throughout this project, shown here generically rather than pulled from ticket.service.js directly (that's the very next topic):

// illustrative — not from this project's code
await prisma.user.findMany();                     // every row
await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: 1 } }); // one row, by a unique field
await prisma.user.create({ data: { name: 'Ada', email: 'ada@example.com' } });

Every one of these returns a Promise — the same async/await from Lesson 1, not new syntax, just a new thing on the other end of it: an actual round trip to MySQL instead of a plain array lookup. findUnique specifically requires its where to target a field marked @id or @unique in the schema (id, or email on User) — Prisma can guarantee at most one matching row for those, which is what makes findUnique return a single object (or null) rather than an array.

One more shape worth knowing before the next topic: include and select, passed alongside where, control what comes back — include pulls in a related model (a ticket's customer, from the relations topics), and select narrows which fields of a model actually get returned, rather than every column. Both matter in ticket.service.js, coming up next.
